extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review of Visual Question Answering (VQA) examining problem formulation, existing datasets, evaluation metrics, and algorithms, with a focus on the limitations of current datasets due to biases and the efficacy of existing algorithms.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafe and Christopher Kanan
extraction.citeAs: Kushal Kafe and Christopher Kanan. Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4 [cs.CV], 2017.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper reviews several datasets. DAQUAR was based on images from the NYU-DepthV2 Dataset. COCO-QA QA pairs were created using an NLP algorithm from COCO image captions. The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA) used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers to generate questions and separate workers for answers. Visual Genome used free-form and region-specific methods prompting workers to ask questions about specific image regions. Visual7W is a subset of Visual Genome.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: NYU-DepthV2 Dataset, Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO) dataset, YFCC100M, Synthetic cartoon imagery
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: In COCO-QA, longer sentences were broken into smaller chunks for ease of processing by the NLP algorithm.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: COCO-VQA: AMT workers asked to 'Stump a smart robot' for questions; separate workers provided 10 answers per question. Visual Genome: Free-form and region-specific question prompting using descriptive bounding-box annotations. Visual7W: Plausible answers collected by prompting annotators to answer without seeing the image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is 83.3%. Lack of consensus is common, especially for 'Why' questions. Multiple correct answers can exist in opposition (e.g., yes/no splits). Consensus metric used: Accuracy VQA = min(n/3, 1).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Age, gender, and races (represented in SYNTH-VQA synthetic human models)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aid to blind and visually impaired individuals; improving human-computer interaction; image retrieval.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Strong language biases allow image-blind algorithms to perform well (e.g., 49.6% on COCO-VQA). Distribution biases exist (e.g., 'yes' is the majority answer for 59% of yes/no questions in COCO-VQA). Annotators tend to ask similar questions about holistic content. Questions often contain language clues that bias the answer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Datasets are often too small (DAQUAR) or contain biases that limit assessment. DAQUAR has exclusively indoor scenes. COCO-QA has grammatical errors and nonsensical questions due to NLP flaws. COCO-VQA contains subjective/opinion-seeking questions and lacks inter-human agreement. Evaluation metrics can be gamed.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of VQA algorithms
